ei.title: 43-45번 — The Feast Is for My Clothes
ei.subject: 9월_2024 고1 모의고사
ei.lesson: 43-45번 — The Feast Is for My Clothes

fullPassage: Once upon a time in the Iranian city of Shiraz, there lived the famous poet Sheikh Saadi. Like most other poets and philosophers, he led a very simple life. A rich merchant of Shiraz was preparing for his daughter's wedding and invited him along with a lot of big businessmen of the town. The poet accepted the invitation and decided to attend. On the day of the wedding, the rich merchant, the host of the wedding, was receiving the guests at the gate. Many rich people of the town attended the wedding. They had come out in their best clothes. The poet wore simple clothes which were neither grand nor expensive. He waited for someone to approach him but no one gave him as much as even a second glance. Even the host did not greet him and looked away. Seeing all this, the poet quietly left the party and went to a shop where he could rent clothes. There he chose a richly decorated coat, which made him look like a new person. With this coat, he entered the party and this time was welcomed with open arms. The host embraced him as he would do to an old friend and complimented him on the clothes he was wearing. The poet did not say a word and allowed the host to lead him to the dining room. The host personally led the poet to his seat and served out chicken soup to him. After a moment, the poet suddenly dipped the corner of his coat in the soup as if he fed it. All the guests were now staring at him in surprise. The host said, "Sir, what are you doing?" The poet very calmly replied, "Now that I have put on expensive clothes, I see a world of difference here. All that I can say now is that this feast is meant for my clothes, not for me."

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 그는 소박한 삶을 살았다. 상인은 그를 초대했다. 시인은 참석하기로 했다. 부자들이 참석했다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 그는 환영받았다. 주인은 그를 껴안았다. 그가 입고 있던 옷. 그는 이끌도록 허락했다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 그는 소박한 삶을 살았다. 상인은 그를 초대했다. 주인은 인사도 없이 외면했다. 시인은 차분하게 대답했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① simple(소박한): 소박한 삶을 살았다는 문맥에 적절
✅ ② invited(초대했다): 상인이 그를 초대했다는 문맥에 적절
❌ ③ scold(꾸짖다) → greet(인사하다): 주인은 소박한 옷차림의 시인에게 '인사(greet)'조차 하지 않고 외면했다는 문맥. scold(꾸짖다)는 부적절
✅ ④ calmly(차분하게): 시인이 차분하게 대답했다는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: did not ___ him and looked away(그를 ~하지 않고 외면했다)의 흐름에는 greet(인사하다)가 자연스럽습니다.

det.korean: 그는 화려하게 장식된 코트를 골랐다. 그는 환영받았다. 주인은 그를 껴안았다. 그는 엄청난 차이를 느꼈다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① richly(화려하게): 화려하게 장식된 코트를 골랐다는 문맥에 적절

✅ ③ embraced(껴안았다): 주인이 오랜 친구처럼 껴안았다는 문맥에 적절
✅ ④ difference(차이): 옷에 따라 대접이 달라진 엄청난 차이를 느꼈다는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: 뒤에 이어지는 embraced(껴안았다)와 어울리려면 welcomed(환영받았다)여야 합니다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 그는 누군가 다가와 주기를 기다렸지만 아무도 그를 한 번 더 쳐다보지조차 않았다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① a single word(한 마디 말): 시선을 강조하는 문맥과 다름
❌ ② any food or drink(어떤 음식이나 음료): 무시당하는 상황과 무관

✅ ④ a second glance(한 번 더 힐끗 봄): 아무도 그를 '한 번 더 쳐다보지'조차 않았다는 문맥에 적절 (as much as even ~로 강조)
det.tip: as much as even ___(~조차)이 단서입니다. 뒤 문장 did not greet(인사조차 안 함)와 연결됩니다.

det.korean: 소박한 옷차림일 때는 아무도 시인을 거들떠보지 않았다.

❌ ① 시인은 대부분의 시인처럼 '소박한(simple)' 삶을 살았음

questions.passage: Once upon a time in the Iranian city of Shiraz, there lived the famous poet Sheikh Saadi. Like most other poets and philosophers, he led a very simple life. A rich merchant of Shiraz was preparing for his daughter's wedding and invited him along with a lot of big businessmen of the town. The poet accepted the invitation and decided to attend. On the day of the wedding, the rich merchant, the host of the wedding, was receiving the guests at the gate. Many rich people of the town attended the wedding. They had come out in their best clothes. The poet wore simple clothes which were neither grand nor expensive. He waited for someone to approach him but no one gave him as much as even a second glance. Even the host did not greet him and looked away. Seeing all this, the poet quietly left the party and went to a shop where he could rent clothes. There he chose a richly decorated coat, which made him look like a new person. With this coat, he entered the party and this time was welcomed with open arms. The host embraced him as he would do to an old friend and complimented him on the clothes he was wearing. The poet did not say a word and __________ to the dining room. The host personally led the poet to his seat and served out chicken soup to him. After a moment, the poet suddenly dipped the corner of his coat in the soup as if he fed it. All the guests were now staring at him in surprise. The host said, "Sir, what are you doing?" The poet very calmly replied, "Now that I have put on expensive clothes, I see a world of difference here. All that I can say now is that this feast is meant for my clothes, not for me."
